method: Build the actual workspace CLI with full+otel and no native default feature, then invoke rust_artifact.sh build-cli and restore-cli. Both revisions differ only in a benchmark note; each CLI and native runtime must report the new revision. Use private per-arm targets and Kache runtimes, 8 build jobs, a 44-GiB scope, ci-cli, and the canonical warnings/mold flags. First measure forced native incremental and artifact-only with codegen units 16; then measure the current CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 policy with no codegen-unit override.
decision: Enable native incremental compilation only for the owned, persistent shared CLI producer, using the measured 16-codegen-unit configuration. Keep workspace tests, package audits, hosted runners, and other crates on their existing policies. The persistent target remains private to its runner and retains the existing 40-GiB ceiling.
limitations: One warm revision rebuild per arm, sequential rather than interleaved. Earlier revision and real native-body-edit trials provide repeated lower-level controls, not repeated full producers.

First CLI builds have unequal pre-existing feature/profile cache state and are not a cold-bootstrap comparison. The initial incremental packaging run was resumed after an invalid public freshness flag failed; its completed build, package, restore and version proof were retained.

The targets contain prior embedding-probe artifacts. The current-policy control reuses the artifact target and retains both codegen configurations, so its target total is not a clean policy storage comparison. The initial incremental storage-before measurement was overwritten on resume and is unmeasured.

Kache report counters are cumulative within a checkout session. Native incremental work is a passthrough and is absent from cache compiler-time totals; Cargo units and command wall times are the timing evidence.
The physical LLM and orchestration cuts are not in these source revisions. End-to-end merge-group p90 against 600 seconds remains unproven.
